task_title: internal/federation hold-manager retry gate is a fixed 20ms sleep
task_criteria:
internal/federation hold-manager retry gate is event-driven with a bounded budget; three claims, all resolvable in this tree.
(A) `go test -count=1 ./internal/federation/` exits 0. This package suite runs in ~4s, inside the judge's 30s command cap.
(B) the retry worker waits on events, not a fixed pre-retry sleep: HoldManager carries `stopCh chan struct{}` and `wakeCh chan struct{}` (internal/federation/hold.go:317-318); `wake()` nudges the buffered channel without blocking (hold.go:442-448); `loop()` selects on stopCh/wakeCh/timer before every Sweep (hold.go:449-470); the wait is bounded by HoldConfig.RetryEvery and MaxRetryInterval (hold.go:286-287), whose zero values fall back to defaults.
(C) non-vacuity is proven in the tests: TestHoldManagerRetryWaitIsNonVacuous (internal/federation/hold_test.go:421) shows the retry observation cannot pass on the synchronous forward alone, and TestHoldManagerRetriesUntilRecoveryDeliversOnce observes the retry through the bounded waitFor helper (hold_test.go:84, used at hold_test.go:380) instead of a bare time.Sleep(20ms).
PROOF: go test -count=1 ./internal/federation/ && grep -n 'wakeCh chan struct{}' internal/federation/hold.go
FAILIF: a fixed time.Sleep gates the retry attempt, wake() blocks or is absent, RetryEvery/MaxRetryInterval do not bound the wait, or either named test is missing or renamed.

items.criterion: The event-driven retry loop is reachable from the server entrypoint: cmd/server/main.go constructs the HoldManager, calls Start() (launching loop()) and Stop() on shutdown.
items.detail: cmd/server/main.go:838-844: `fedHold = federation.NewHoldManager(fedClient, holdQueue, federation.HoldConfig{MaxHold: cfg.Federation.MaxHold})`, then `fedHold.Start()` and `defer fedHold.Stop()`. Start() (hold.go:381-391) launches `go m.loop()`; Stop() (hold.go:398-407) closes stopCh and waits on the WaitGroup. RetryEvery/MaxRetryInterval are left zero here and filled by withDefaults (hold.go:292-301), so the production path uses the event-driven loop with default bounds.

items.criterion: wake() cannot block or panic: buffered cap-1 channel + select/default, never closed, so it is safe before Start and after Stop.
items.detail: hold.go:442-448 `func (m *HoldManager) wake() { select { case m.wakeCh <- struct{}{}: default: } }` over the cap-1 buffered channel created at hold.go:330; the channel is never closed (only stopCh is closed, hold.go:405), so a wake after Stop cannot panic and a full buffer cannot block. Called from Enqueue at hold.go:436.

items.criterion: The retry wait is bounded: loop() resets a timer to cfg.RetryEvery each pass (hold.go:451,467) and per-item backoff delay() is capped at MaxRetryInterval (hold.go:490-492), so no unbounded wait exists.
items.detail: hold.go:451 `timer := time.NewTimer(m.cfg.RetryEvery)`; after each Sweep the timer is drained and `timer.Reset(m.cfg.RetryEvery)` (hold.go:461-467); per-item backoff `delay()` (hold.go:482-495) doubles RetryEvery but clamps `if d > m.cfg.MaxRetryInterval || d <= 0 { d = m.cfg.MaxRetryInterval }` (hold.go:491-492). Zero config values are replaced by DefaultRetryEvery=2s / DefaultMaxRetryInterval=60s (hold.go:41-44, 292-301), so every wait is bounded.
